most_damaging: D1 — the opening thesis reverses the direction of its own first correction and claims a 'near-cancellation' that the body's own arithmetic (1.48x numerator, 7.6x denominator, 5.4x net fall) contradicts.

findings.location: Opening thesis — 'The two largest errors point in opposite directions: the link is faster than the model assumes once the right column is read... They nearly cancel'
findings.issue: The thesis misstates the direction of the first correction and overstates the cancellation. The body says the numerator grows 1.48x (communication is slower than the model assumes), not faster; and the net effect is a 5.4x fall in overhead (36% to 6.6%), not a near-cancellation. The 'which is why the conclusion looks sound' causal story is therefore false: the conclusion looks sound because the denominator correction dominates, not because the errors cancel.
findings.evidence: [[interim-report-allreduce-ceiling-and-definition]] establishes that the busbw reading makes algbw 0.503 GB/s, so the payload takes 3.98 s rather than 2.7 s — communication is slower, not faster. The report's own DDP Overhead Model says 'The numerator grows 1.48x' and 'the ratio falls 5.4x'. comparisons.md says the net effect is 'from the repo's 36% to ~4%', not a cancellation. The report's own table gives 7.1% for the busbw reading, not 6.6%.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the thesis sentence to say: 'The two errors point in opposite directions: the all-reduce is slower than the model assumes once the right column is read, and the step is far longer than the model assumes once attention is counted. The second correction dominates, so the overhead falls 5.4x — which is why the conclusion looks sound, and why the program cannot tell when it has stopped being sound.' Do not claim the errors 'nearly cancel'; say the denominator correction dominates and the numerator correction partially offsets it.

findings.location: Opening thesis and DDP Overhead Model — 'DDP's gradient all-reduce costs roughly 6.6% of step time (T4)' and 'The derived 6.6% is the conservative figure'
findings.issue: The 6.6% is a T4 arithmetic estimate derived from a three-card Gen2 x16 measurement scaled by width and efficiency, with no five-rank measurement, yet the report uses it to adjudicate topologies as if it were a T1 measurement. The report's own Hardware Reality section gives an algbw band of 0.58-0.67 GB/s (5.3-6.1%), its own table gives 7.1% for the busbw reading and 11.4% for Gen1 x4, and the 6.6% uses a 0.53 GB/s algbw that is below the report's own calibrated band. The report also says 'The 36% is reproducible from the plan's own inputs' without noting that this is only true under the algbw reading the report rejects.
findings.evidence: [[interim-report-allreduce-ceiling-and-definition]] gives the x4 algbw band as 0.584-0.671 GB/s (0.544-0.625 GiB/s), which yields 5.3-6.1% against 56.3 s, not 6.6%. The report's own table row '32k, 450 TFLOPS, busbw reading (3.2 GB wire at 0.805 GB/s)' gives 7.1%, and 'Gen1 x4 busbw (~0.5 GB/s)' gives 11.4%. [[readmemd]] is a three-card Gen2 x16 receipt with 'One probe run per pair; no cross-run error bars'; [[2026-10-01-cmp170hx-4card-bar1-p2p-plx-cudaipynb]] is four cards. [[why-is-the-bandwidth-utilization-of-7-gpus-much-lower-than-that-of-6-8-gpus-for]] records an NCCL maintainer confirming 5- and 7-GPU runs are 'much lower than others' due to offset alignment, so the N=5 penalty may exceed the 1.6x ring-load factor.
findings.recommendation: Replace the point estimate with a range and label it T4: 'At Gen2 x4 the overhead is 5.3-7.1% depending on whether the plan's number is read as algbw or busbw; at Gen1 x4 it is 11.4%; at Gen2 x16 it is 1.5%. The 6.6% point estimate is a T4 extrapolation from a three-card x16 receipt, not a five-rank measurement, and the N=5 alignment penalty is unmeasured.' In the Verdict, say 'DDP's overhead is single-digit percent at Gen2 x4' rather than '6.6%'. Add a sentence noting that the 36% is reproducible only under the algbw reading the report rejects; under the busbw reading it is 54-58% at the plan's denominator.

findings.location: Opening thesis — 'What binds is wall-clock: 90-100 TFLOPS per card sustained (T1/T2)... which turns a planned 25-hour run into 3-7 days'
findings.issue: The 'wall-clock is binding' claim is not defined against a threshold and is undermined by the report's own 14-39k tok/s band: at the upper end 9B tokens is 2.7 days, and the experiment is feasible as planned. The report's own band includes the interim report's 'too pessimistic' threshold (>25k tok/s), and the report never engages that possibility. The binding constraint is the multi-arm program, not the single 9B run.
findings.evidence: [[interim-report-sustained-throughput-at-32k]] says 'If a measured 32k run hit >25k tok/s on 5 cards (>640 TFLOPS aggregate model-FLOPs, >63% MFU), my centre estimate would be too pessimistic by ~1.7x'. The report's own band is '14-39k tok/s, centre 20-27k'; at 39k, 9e9/39e3 = 2.7 days; at 27k, 3.9 days; at 20k, 5.2 days. The repo's plan is 25 hours, so 3-7 days is 3-7x the plan, but the experiment is still feasible. [[readmemd-faircslmtrainbench-at-main]] measures 63.88% MFU at 32k, which supports the upper end.
findings.recommendation: Define the threshold: 'Wall-clock is binding against the repo's 25-hour plan, not against feasibility: at the top of the 14-39k tok/s band the 9B run is 2.7 days and the experiment is feasible as planned; at the bottom it is 7.4 days. The binding constraint is the multi-arm program, not the single run.' Add a sentence acknowledging that the interim report's >25k tok/s threshold would make its centre estimate ~1.7x too pessimistic, and that the report's own band includes that region.

findings.location: The compute ladder — '91-100 TFLOPS | unlocked, 250 W | end-to-end training, ~4k ctx | T1'
findings.issue: The report's T1 sustained denominator (91-100 TFLOPS/card) is contradicted by the repo's own 140k tok/s baseline: at 4k with hidden 2048, 140k tok/s implies 162 TFLOPS/card (80% MFU); with the report's corrected hidden 1216, it implies 130 TFLOPS/card (64% MFU). The interim report flagged this as an open question; the final report dropped it. The only receipted sustained anchor is the 180 W burn at 74.6-78.5 TFLOPS/card.
findings.evidence: [[interim-report-sustained-throughput-at-32k]]: 'The repo's triple (140k tok/s, 494M, "inferred ~4k") is internally inconsistent with its own 91-100 TFLOPS/GPU claim: at 4k with attention counted the baseline implies 163 TFLOPS/GPU (80% MFU, implausible); at 91-100 TFLOPS/GPU it implies ~400-880 tokens of context.' The repo's own baseline is '494M Qwen3-architecture model, 9B tokens ... ~21 h at ~140k tok/s on 5 GPUs (91-100 TFLOPS/GPU)'. The report's own correction says 'A physically consistent 494M/28-layer model has hidden ~1216'; at hidden 1216 and 4k, 140k tok/s implies 130 TFLOPS/card, still above 91-100. [[readmemd-2]] and [[2026-09-02-cmp170hx-health-gateipynb]] are the only receipted sustained measurements (74.6-78.5 at 180 W).
findings.recommendation: Either use the 140k tok/s baseline as the T1 anchor (which raises the throughput band to 130-162 TFLOPS/card and shortens the 9B run to 2-3 days), or flag the inconsistency explicitly: 'The repo's 91-100 TFLOPS/card figure is inconsistent with its own 140k tok/s baseline at 4k; the only receipted sustained anchor is the 180 W burn at 74.6-78.5 TFLOPS/card, and the 250 W sustained rate is unmeasured.' Do not present 91-100 as a settled T1 figure.

findings.location: MoE & EP — 'So EP is out because no training-grade EP implementation exists for a no-P2P, no-NVLink, no-RDMA fabric — a software fact, not a physical one.'
findings.issue: This is absence-of-evidence presented as evidence-of-absence. The report's source says the EP libraries rely on NVLink/P2P/RDMA 'for their optimized GPU-initiated paths', not that they cannot run at all; the corpus contains PCIe-native all-to-all scheduling (VarioPath) and host-staged training communication (HFReduce, LLMQ), and the report straw-mans VarioPath as 'inference-only' because it lacks a backward pass, which a collective scheduler would not have.
findings.evidence: [[efficient-expert-parallel-communication]] body: 'Communication libraries specialized for MoE EP ... similarly rely on NVLink, GPUDirect P2P, or RDMA for their optimized GPU-initiated paths.' The same note lists HFReduce ('CPU-based All-Reduce for gradients') and LLMQ ('dense weight and gradient transfers for low-precision pretraining') as host-memory training communication implementations. [[variopath-workload-aware-all-to-all-communication-for-pcie-gpu-clusters]] is 'workload-aware AlltoAllv scheduling for PCIe GPU clusters — the primitive that EP dispatch/combine and sequence parallelism are built from'; the report dismisses it as an 'inference-only sibling' and says 'none of them ships a backward pass'. [[memory-efficient-expert-routing-for-distributed-moe]] is a training method but relies on NVLink P2P, so it does not port.
findings.recommendation: Replace the absolute claim with an absence-of-evidence claim: 'The corpus contains no evidence of an integrated training-grade EP framework for this fabric. The closest are VarioPath, a PCIe-native all-to-all scheduler evaluated on inference, and ThunderEP, a no-P2P dispatch/combine with no backward; both are systems projects to port, not hardware impossibilities. The primitive exists — HFReduce and LLMQ already do host-staged gradient communication — but no EP training loop has been built on it.'

findings.location: What the link delivers to a collective — 'Read as algbw it implies a busbw of 1.29 GB/s, which is 77% of the one-way rate... The busbw reading is the one the evidence supports'
findings.issue: The report dismisses the algbw reading too quickly: its source's confidence is medium (~72%), the repo's 494M/140k tok/s datapoint weakly favours algbw, and the 'no P2P' premise that makes algbw implausible is itself unverified. The report treats a 72%-confidence inference as a settled fact and drops the caveat that if BAR1 P2P is live, the algbw reading becomes plausible and the whole locus flips. It also says 'only one is physically possible' when the algbw reading is merely above the best measured efficiency, not physically impossible.
findings.evidence: [[interim-report-allreduce-ceiling-and-definition]]: 'Confidence: medium (~72%) ... the repo's single 494M/140k tok/s datapoint weakly favours the algbw reading without being able to discriminate it.' It also says: 'If BAR1 P2P is live on the box, the algbw reading becomes plausible and the whole locus flips' and 'the repo says "no P2P" but does not say how it was established. If it was established by cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer alone, that is exactly the test the club shows returns 0 even when cuMemcpyPeer succeeds via host staging.' [[github-bayleycmpunlocker-a-cmpunlocker-fork-with-working-p2p-on-sys-4028gr-trt2]] shows P2P works at 1.68 GB/s each way at Gen2 x4 on 12/12 pairs. [[p2pmd]] says P2P is absent by default but the patch half-works.
findings.recommendation: Add a qualifier: 'The busbw reading is a 72%-confidence inference, not a measurement. The repo's 494M/140k tok/s datapoint weakly favours the algbw reading, and if the box's "no P2P" claim is a software-configuration statement rather than a hardware one — cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer returns 0 even when cuMemcpyPeer succeeds via host staging — the algbw reading becomes plausible and the overhead doubles. The pre-flight should establish P2P status with cuMemcpyPeer, not cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer alone.' Replace 'only one is physically possible' with 'only one is consistent with the best measured efficiency'.

findings.location: Engram & Frozen Memory — 'Freezing the tables does not merely save memory; it removes the collective entirely: no all-to-all, no gradient dispatch... The frozen-table design is the only Engram variant that keeps the architecture off the wire.'
findings.issue: The report conflates freezing with replication. Freezing removes the gradient collective; replication removes the forward gather collective. The report's budget assumes the table is replicated at 24.58 GB/card, which is what eliminates the forward all-to-all. A frozen but sharded table would cost ~4.9 GB/card but reintroduce the forward all-to-all. The report's claim that freezing alone 'removes the collective entirely' is therefore false for the sharded variant, which is the memory-cheaper one.
findings.evidence: [[conditional-memory-via-scalable-lookup]]: 'tables are sharded across available GPUs. An All-to-All communication primitive is employed ... to gather active rows in the forward pass and dispatch gradients in the backward pass.' Freezing removes the backward dispatch but not the forward gather if the table remains sharded. [[memory-grafting-scaling-language-model]] says the frozen table is ~12 GB per layer and the recipient carries two grafted layers, so the replicated total is 24.58 GB/card — the memory cost that buys the collective elimination.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish the two mechanisms: 'Freezing removes the gradient collective; replicating the table removes the forward gather collective. The design needs both: a frozen table that is also replicated at 24.58 GB/card. A frozen but sharded table would cost ~4.9 GB/card and leave ~16 GB more headroom, but it would reintroduce the forward all-to-all at one-fifth the volume. The report should state this trade-off rather than attributing the collective elimination to freezing alone.'

findings.location: Training Topologies — 'TP=5 | ... | Yes | Ruled out on placement' and 'TP is out for a placement reason rather than a bandwidth one... TP has no equivalent hiding place.'
findings.issue: The report says TP is 'ruled out' when its own table says TP fits 7B on 64 GB and costs 2.8x, and its own source shows TP overtaking DP for 20B+ models on PCIe. A 2.8x overhead is a cost, not a feasibility block; the report straw-mans TP as unavailable when it is merely dominated. The 'placement' framing conflates 'the collectives are on the critical path' with 'the topology cannot be used'.
findings.evidence: [[efficient-training-on-multiple-consumer-gpus-with]] measures Megatron-TP on 8x RTX 4090 PCIe 4.0 and finds 'For larger models (20B+), TP and PP overtake DP by avoiding full-parameter synchronization'; it also says Megatron-TP's throughput 'becomes impractical under PCIe' at small scale, which is a cost statement, not a feasibility one. The report's own table row says 'TP=5 ... 126 GB ... ~2.8x ... Yes ... Ruled out on placement' — 'Yes' means it fits 7B on 64 GB. [[on-optimizing-the-communication-of-model-parallelism]] shows model-parallel communication can be overlapped with compute via an overlap-friendly pipeline schedule, which weakens 'TP has no equivalent hiding place'.
findings.recommendation: Restate as 'TP is feasible but dominated': 'TP=5 fits 7B on 64 GB and costs ~2.8x at 1B; it is not ruled out by the fabric, but it is dominated by ZeRO-2 and PP=5 for this model size. At 20B+ on PCIe, TP can overtake DP by avoiding full-parameter synchronization, so the "ruled out" framing is too strong.' Remove 'Ruled out on placement' from the table and replace it with 'Feasible, dominated'.
